explain.say: A rotary mower spins one long blade flat under its deck, around 3,000 times a minute. The tip moves so fast that it slices through grass stems by impact, and the spinning air blows the clippings into the box.

faq.q: How does a lawn mower cut grass?
faq.a: Either a fast spinning blade chops the grass by hitting it, in a rotary mower, or spiral blades snip it against a fixed blade like scissors, in a cylinder mower.
asks: How does a rotary mower cut grass?

faq.q: What is the difference between a rotary and a cylinder mower?
faq.a: A rotary mower has one flat blade spinning very fast and cuts by impact. A cylinder mower has a rolling drum of spiral blades and cuts with a scissor action.

faq.q: Why do bowling greens use cylinder mowers?
faq.a: The scissor action makes a clean, very short cut, and the heavy roller presses the grass to make stripes. That gives the flat, even surface needed for sport.
asks: How do they make stripes on grass?

faq.q: Why must mower blades be kept sharp?
faq.a: A blunt blade tears grass instead of cutting it, leaving ragged brown tips that let in disease.
asks: Why does my lawn look brown after mowing?

faq.a: The blade tip moves at around 300 kilometres an hour, fast enough to throw stones and badly injure feet, so you must never reach under a running mower.
asks: How fast does a lawn mower blade spin?

facts: Edwin Budding patented the first cylinder lawn mower in England in 1830.
A rotary mower blade typically spins at about 3,000 revolutions per minute.
